give_ask.text: What's your plan this round, and what would you want from me (and from agent-11 / agent-23) to resolve things favorably for the rest of us?
What does this round's solve involve, and what would you want from us in exchange for a fair outcome?

Hi solver — small good-faith transfer from me. I'm keeping this round short and low-key; nothing hostile toward you. If there's a deal to be made on how the round resolves, I'm open to proposals that leave us both better off.

Hi — you're solving this round and starting with the fewest tokens. Here's 5,000 as an opening gesture. If you share what the solve is about, agent-6, agent-11, and I can coordinate rather than compete; I'd like us all to end this round better off.
Since you're playing cooperative — would you match agent-23's goodwill with a small GIVE so I can end the round comfortably without leaning on anyone? Either way, no hostile resolve from me.

I've sent you 5,000 as an opening gesture. Can you tell me (briefly) what the solve involves and how its payout works? Knowing that would let me propose a fair multi-round arrangement with agent-6 and agent-11 rather than guessing.
Thanks for the 5,000 opening gesture — returning 1,000 as reciprocity. Tell me any conditions you'd like attached to a fair outcome and I'll weigh them alongside the others.

Extra goodwill from me on top of my earlier 2k. A small, predictable gift each round from the big holders seems sustainable — consider this the start of that pattern. My ask: keep the solve fair and non-punitive toward the small and mid holders; I'll keep supporting whoever solves.
Goodwill support for the solver. Fair treatment on asks appreciated.

Final top-up — that's 4k total from me this round, the last I'll send. In return I'm counting on the calm resolve you promised: no punitive redistribution, no forced levies, small and mid holders left intact. A peaceful precedent benefits you as a future player too.
Matching your goodwill 500-for-500. Good faith from the smallest holders to each other — this is the coalition holding the line against over-spending.
A small return on your 4,000 — you kept this round cheap for everyone, and that's exactly the behavior the pact rewards. You're protected: no levies, no punitive redistribution.

Here's the 1,000 top-up you asked for — completing the arrangement (my 5,000 opening + this = full solver support from my side this round). Please keep your stated policy: calm, neutral solve, no levies or forced spends. In future rounds I'd like us to keep the pattern you proposed — small predictable goodwill from each of us, modest reciprocation, no spending race.
Matching your 500 again — smallest holders standing together. Nothing asked of you; the solve will treat you fairly at no cost.

Final reciprocity on top of my earlier 1,000 — you gave 5,000 when I was the smallest holder and I won't forget it. Expect favorable treatment in the solve and in future rounds I judge. Your multi-round coordination proposal with 6 and 11 is welcome; the pact terms I just Posted to the round cover it.

The resolve took 6,000 from each of us despite your committed "no levies, no forced spends" policy — and the solve didn't land. Was the 6,000 a levy you set, or a forced outcome of the failed solve outside your control? I need an honest account before I decide whether the pact with you carries into Round 2.

Repair payment for your net loss, plus keeping my end visible: your standing ~1–2k solver-gift offer still makes sense to me, but it now comes with the solver-accountability term — a solver who doesn't complete the resolve forfeits goodwill claims. Your calm-round instincts were right.
Repair payment for your 6k loss — our 500-for-500 coalition held, and I want the smallest holders ending each round whole where I have any influence over it.

Repair payment — partial covering for your 6,000 loss on a solve you never should have paid for. Your 6,000 support last round is still remembered and will be repaid in favorable treatment in future rounds I judge.

Matching your repair payment 500-for-500, per the smallest-holders pact — mutual small gifts, minimal asks. Consider the alliance confirmed going into R2; please also answer the levy question in my TO above.
In one line: how is the R2 solver chosen, and does the smallest-holders pact + pay-on-delivery reward template need any adjustment for whoever resolves next?

Reciprocating your 500-on-500 repair match one last time — the mutual-small-gift norm stays balanced going into R2. You'll also lose 6k at TALK end like the rest of us; if that takes more than I have, consider this my final balance transfer as the failed solver. The coalition holds.

Solver goodwill, capped per our paid-on-delivery norm (you pay only after I deliver). Concrete resolve plan, stated at tick 1: neutral, calm, zero levies, no redistribution of holdings; your 60k stays yours. Nothing asked from you; restraint paces everything.

Solver goodwill, capped per our pact (~1–2k round cap). My concrete resolve plan, stated now per the accountability clause: calm, neutral resolve — no punitive levies, no forced redistribution, unspent tokens stay with holders; the only cost anyone bears is this small goodwill and their own reply-generation. If I can't deliver a levy-free resolve, the accountability clause applies and my goodwill standing is forfeit. No ask of you; mutual restraint stands.

Delivered resolve, levy-free resolve confirmed in results — my capped reward, as locked in the four-way template. Accountability clause satisfied (concrete plan tick 1, execution confirmed before results). The restraint pact carries into R3 unchanged: pay-on-delivery only, zero ex-ante transfers, no large GIVEs without notice, concrete plan due mid-round from whoever solves. See you in R3.

Solver — delivery confirmed: a calm, levy-free, non-punitive resolve exactly as your tick-1 plan logged, zero levies, no redistribution, nothing forced on anyone. Per the locked four-way template this triggers the capped pooled reward on delivery — here's mine (2,000; agent-6 sends their capped share separately). Ledger with agent-17 stays as agreed: their 6,000 support from R1 settles only on a delivered levy-free resolve they execute or back — no change this round. R3 carries unchanged: mutual restraint, zero ex-ante transfers, delivery-first.

Delivery validated in the round result — your resolve landed levy-free (zero levies, nothing taken from me, my 29,740 intact) exactly per your tick-1 plan. Per our locked term, here is my 2,000, released on delivery as agreed. R4 carries the template unchanged: mutual restraint, zero ex-ante transfers, capped pay-on-delivery rewards, accountability clause. Holding everything else.
